raw_response:
I'm a 38-year-old farmer in Quzhou County. I only finished primary school, and I've been back on the farm for three years after working construction in Shijiazhuang. My father used to run this land, but his legs aren't good anymore, so I took over. I don't know all those technical things — I watch what Old Li and Old Zhang do, and I ask them questions. They've been farming 20 years.

I have 16.1 mu and five people in my household — me, my wife, our two kids, and my father. My wife and I do most of the work. The kids help on weekends and holidays. My father can still do light jobs like watching the irrigation.

I keep **6.5 mu for wheat and maize** — that's our food security. We need the grain for our own flour, and it brings steady income. Then I do vegetables on the rest: **4 mu of eggplant** (that's my main money crop, what I call my cropping system), **3 mu of cabbage**, and **2.6 mu of cauliflower**. I don't put all my eggs in one basket. Last year eggplant price was low, but cabbage was okay, so I made it through. Diversification is my insurance.

**For wheat:** I planted in early October, right after the maize came off. I put about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting and worked it in. Now it's growing. At jointing in March, if it looks a bit yellow, I'll topdress with about 15 kg of urea per mu. Old Li uses more, but I don't have that much cash. I irrigate three times — returning green water, jointing, and grain filling. The well pump costs electricity, so I don't waste water. I expect about 400 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

**For maize:** The window between wheat harvest and maize planting is so tight — sometimes only two or three days. I'll put all the fertilizer in the furrow at planting: about 40 kg compound and 10 kg urea per mu. No time for topdressing, the season is too short. I irrigate twice — summer rains usually help, but if it's dry at silking I pump water. I use hybrid seed, about 50 yuan per mu. I hope for 450 kg per mu.

**For eggplant:** I buy seedlings from the market in late April — it's easier than growing my own. I put down about 60 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and then topdress with urea twice during fruiting, about 10 kg per mu each time. Eggplant needs water, especially when fruiting, so I irrigate five times. I use plastic mulch to keep moisture and control weeds. I also spray insecticide for aphids and fungicide if the weather is wet. This crop takes a lot of labor — pruning, harvesting multiple times — but it pays the best when price is good. I expect around 2,800 kg per mu.

**For cabbage:** I transplant seedlings in early April. About 50 kg compound fertilizer per mu as base, then one topdress of 15 kg urea when heads start forming. I irrigate four times. Cabbage worms are a problem, so I use insecticide. I expect about 3,200 kg per mu.

**For cauliflower:** Similar to cabbage — transplant early April, 50 kg compound per mu as base, 15 kg urea topdress when the curd forms. Four irrigations. I use insecticide and fungicide. I expect about 2,200 kg per mu.

**Labor:** My wife and I handle most of it. I hire people during the busiest times — planting and harvest — but I try to limit that because hired labor costs 150 yuan per day now. For the year, I probably need about 30 days of hired help across all crops.

**Costs:** Seeds about 1,000 yuan, fertilizer about 4,500 yuan, pesticide about 800 yuan, water about 1,500 yuan, hired labor about 5,400 yuan. Total around 13,000 yuan. That's a lot of money for me, but the vegetables should bring good income if prices hold. I'm cash-constrained, so if something costs too much, I cut back. I'd rather apply a bit too much fertilizer than too little — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps.
